newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex lauds spread on latest Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Pemex lauds spread on latest Eurobond.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) on Wednesday lauded the spread it received on its lastest Eurobond, a 10-year 750 billion lira step-up issue.

The Mexican oil giant said the spread on the bond was 30 basis points better than on its 10-year $250 million Eurobond issued in May at 223 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, once swapped into dollars at a fixed rate.
The company added the spread on its latest Eurobond was better than the one Argentina received on its last bond in the same market.

The lastest Pemex Eurobond, worth about $425 million, will pay 10.125 percent annual in the first two years and 7.375 percent after that, or 150 basis points over the swap rate in liras for the same maturities.
It will also be convertible to Euros in the third step of the European Monetary Union, the oil company said.

"It is important to underline that the placement of the Pemex paper in the market took place 10 basis points under the level of the Argentine bond launched in this region two weeks ago, which reflects the acceptance the European market has for Petroleos Mexicanos and the perception of Mexico in international financial markets," Pemex said in a statement.
The bond was originally scheduled to be for 500 billion liras but was bumped up to 750 billion lira on good demand, it said.
The last time Pemex went to the lira market was in March, when it placed a 350 billion lira seven-year Eurobond. It has also been busy placing Eurobonds denominatd in dollars.
